title: What does a soil-water point measure?
subtitle: Follow an observation from a source row to a plot—and keep assumptions separate.
summary: Explore 278 laboratory observations from three samples in one plot at Prairie du Sac, Wisconsin. Compare raw points, inspect instrument labels, and try a separate synthetic storage calculation.
audience: Curious general readers; no specialist background required.
scope: A descriptive single-plot subset, not a controlled depth experiment, fitted retention curve or irrigation recommendation.
author: atlas-editor

rights.scope: Selected all three plot 1 samples, projected eight columns, preserved decimal strings and row order. Plot x positions use log10; values and tables remain raw. No fitted data or imported figures.

passages.title: The unit of observation
passages.text: A row records a reported water-content value and water-potential magnitude for a named sample and instrument. A sample contributes many such rows.
passages.context: Original explanation based on the pinned CSV and its metadata. The full file has 1,106 rows from 12 samples; this page retains all 278 rows from the three reported depths in plot 1. These are not 278 independent field samples.

claims.text: Two distinct observations can have the same water-potential magnitude within a sample.
claims.qualification: For US-DFC_1_000, source rows 902 and 904 both report 1.0471285 MPa, with water contents 19.12% and 12.21%. Retain both; no averaging or correction is inferred.

claims.text: The displayed samples can be compared descriptively.
claims.qualification: These observations do not isolate a causal depth effect or represent the whole site.

context: Reported water content (%) is the source column Vol_Water. The available metadata says “Sample Water Content (%)” without explicitly defining volume/volume. This page does not convert those measurements into storage.

Water-potential magnitude, MPa, displays the positive source MPa_Abs values. The metadata describes negative water potential; the chart shows magnitude, not positive signed potential. MPa is a pressure unit.

The chart spaces magnitudes using log10: equal distances represent equal ratios. Raw magnitudes remain available in the point readout and full tables. Points are unconnected; repeated x values remain separate observations.
Hypropfilter is an instrument code: 1 = WP4C; 2 = HyProp. It is not a quality flag. No calibration or measurement-uncertainty audit is claimed.
Density is omitted because its documented units conflict with the values. Conductivity is omitted; its caution flags do not constitute a blanket rating of retention rows.

The local audit uses frozen original metadata and hash-matched CSVs. The later API check was inaccessible, so no fresh remote verification is claimed. Soil-science unit interpretation and representative sampling remain open publication questions.

reviewLimitations: Local review covers source fidelity, evidence labeling and bounded prototype reuse. No professional specialist, screen-reader or learner session has been performed.

selection.rationale: All observed retention rows from the three reported depths in plot 1; illustrative within one plot, not a representative site sample or controlled experiment.

dataset.sourceRowConvention: 1-based CSV line including header; all selected numeric fields retain source decimal strings

activity.transfer: Choose two observed rows and describe exactly what differs. Then explain why neither a difference between depths nor the synthetic 60 mm example tells a farmer when to irrigate.
rubric: Name sample, source row, instrument, units and the observed values.
Distinguish row count from independent sample count, and an x-axis transformation from a new measurement.
Keep repeated magnitudes and their distinct observations visible.
State the synthetic fractions, uniform layer and metre-to-millimetre conversion separately from the dataset.
Identify missing information before applying a result to another site or crop.
